subject: Chi Square Test for  Ordinal Data

messages.author: 07b30bd9f417ebf2
messages.subject: Chi Square Test for  Ordinal Data
parts:
Dear all,

I am running a CFA model using lavaan (version 0.6.16), with ordinal items and the ULS estimator. The model converged regularly after 89 iterations and I did not receive any errors or warnings.

However, I am encountering two issues I’d appreciate help with:

  1. The Chi-square test statistic is reported, but the p-value is NA (as is the p-value for the baseline model).

  2. The standard errors for the residual variances are all zero. Is this expected behavior with ULS and ordinal indicators?

Additionally, I would like to test for residual invariance across groups (or time). Is this feasible under these settings (ordinal data and ULS estimation), and if so, what is the proper way to specify it in lavaan?

Thank you in advance for your help!

Best regards,
Marco

parts: I am running a CFA model using lavaan (version 0.6.16)
To make sure this is an issue with the current software, can you update to the lavaan currently available on CRAN?  Please also provide a reprex.

I would like to test for residual invariance across groups (or time). Is this feasible under these settings (ordinal data and ULS estimation), and if so, what is the proper way to specify it in lavaan?

Yes, if you first establish threshold invariance (for items with > 2 categories) or scalar invariance (for items with only 2 categories).  The syntax is tricky, but the semTools::measEq.syntax() function was designed to help you write the syntax.

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Chi Square Test for Ordinal Data
parts:
On 4/1/25 8:42 AM, Marco Lauriola (ML) wrote:
> 1. The Chi-square test statistic is reported, but the *p-value is NA*
> (as is the p-value for the baseline model).

Did you explicitly use estimator = "ULS"? That would explain it. Change
it to estimator = "ULSMV", or add the arguments se = "robust" and test =
"scaled.shifted".

> 2. The *standard errors for the residual variances are all zero*. Is
> this expected behavior with ULS and ordinal indicators?

That is due to the 'delta' parameterization. The residual variances are
no longer free parameters, but chosen so that the total variances of the
'y-star' variables is unity. An alternative is parameterization = "theta".

Yves.
